scheme_name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)
short_description: Centrally sponsored health assurance scheme providing up to ₹5 Lakhs per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalization.
purpose: Provide financial protection and cashless healthcare access to vulnerable families against catastrophic medical expenses.
geographical_coverage: Pan-India (Nationwide coverage across all participating states and union territories).
eligible_groups: Deprived rural households based on SECC 2011 criteria
Identified occupational categories of urban workers' families
Active National Food Security Act (NFSA) / Ration Card beneficiaries recognized by state criteria
All senior citizens aged 70 years and above (Ayushman Vay Vandana Card)
income_criteria: Targeted at economically vulnerable populations; eligibility primarily derived from SECC database and state-defined NFSA BPL lists.
beneficiary_requirements: Aadhaar card for individual identity verification
Ration Card or Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY Family ID / SECC confirmation
Valid active phone number
covered_treatments: Oncology / Cancer surgeries and chemotherapy
Cardiology and cardiothoracic surgeries (angioplasty, bypass)
Nephrology and kidney care
Orthopedic joint replacements and trauma surgeries
Neurosurgery
General tertiary and secondary surgical procedures (over 1,900 medical packages)
benefits: Cashless and paperless benefit coverage up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year on a family floater basis across empaneled public and private hospitals nationwide.
limitations_and_exclusions: Outpatient department (OPD) consultations, cosmetic surgeries, non-empaneled hospitals (except emergencies), and unlisted elective procedures are not covered.
required_documents: Aadhaar Card (or other government-approved photo ID)
Ration Card (PHH / BPL / AAY) showing family member listing
Existing PM-JAY Golden Card / Ayushman Card (if previously issued)
application_steps: Step 1: Check your family eligibility status on the official portal (beneficiary.nha.gov.in) using your mobile number and Aadhaar.
Step 2: Visit the nearest Ayushman Bharat kiosk, Common Service Centre (CSC), or Arogya Mitra desk at any empaneled hospital.
Step 3: Complete biometric e-KYC using Aadhaar and family ration card verification.
Step 4: Receive your instant Ayushman Card / Golden Card.
Step 5: Present the card at the empaneled hospital helpdesk before admission for cashless pre-authorization.
application_method: Arogya Mitra Helpdesk at empaneled hospitals, Common Service Centres (CSC), or self-registration on NHA Beneficiary Portal.

short_description: Karnataka integrated state health scheme offering cashless treatment up to ₹5 Lakhs for BPL families and financial assistance up to ₹1.5 Lakhs (30% co-share) for APL families.
purpose: Provide universal health coverage to residents of Karnataka through an integrated portal administered by the Suvarna Arogya Suraksha Trust (SAST).
geographical_coverage: Karnataka State (Requires Karnataka residency or domicile).
eligible_groups: Eligible Patients (Category A): BPL / PHH / Anthyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) ration cardholders
General Patients (Category B): APL ration cardholders or residents without BPL cards
income_criteria: Category A: Below Poverty Line (full cashless benefits). Category B: Above Poverty Line (co-payment model with 30% financial concession).
beneficiary_requirements: Karnataka residency (Food and Civil Supplies Department Ration Card)
Aadhaar Card
Referral letter from a Public Health Facility (District/Taluk Hospital) for complex tertiary care in private empaneled hospitals
covered_treatments: Complex tertiary care including oncology, cardiac surgery, and neurosurgery
Specified secondary surgical procedures
Emergency medical stabilizing treatments (direct walk-in allowed without referral)
Neonatal intensive care and pediatric surgeries
benefits: Category A (BPL): Up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year cashless. Category B (APL): 30% assistance of government package rates up to ₹1,50,000 per family per year.
limitations_and_exclusions: Tertiary treatment at private empaneled hospitals strictly requires a referral from a public government hospital (BMCRI, District Hospital), unless it is classified as a life-threatening acute emergency.
required_documents: Aadhaar Card of the patient and family head
Karnataka Ration Card (BPL / PHH / AAY or APL card)
Public Hospital Referral Letter / SAST Referral Slip (for private hospital admissions)
Hospital diagnostic reports and treatment cost estimate
application_steps: Step 1: Visit a government primary/taluk or district hospital (e.g., Victoria Hospital / KC General Hospital in Bengaluru).
Step 2: Approach the Arogya Mitra Helpdesk with your Aadhaar and Karnataka Ration Card to generate your ArK Patient ID.
Step 3: Consult the government hospital specialist. If treatment cannot be provided in-house, the medical officer issues an online SAST referral.
Step 4: Report to the empaneled private or autonomous network hospital with the referral code.
Step 5: The hospital Arogya Mitra submits an online pre-authorization request to SAST for cashless admission.
application_method: Arogya Mitra helpdesk at participating Karnataka government health institutions and empaneled network hospitals.

short_description: Central government financial assistance up to ₹15 Lakhs for BPL patients suffering from life-threatening diseases receiving treatment in government super-specialty hospitals.
purpose: Provide one-time direct financial grant to indigent patients suffering from major life-threatening diseases for treatment at designated central/state government institutes.
geographical_coverage: Pan-India (Requires treatment in designated Central Government super-specialty institutes or state medical colleges).
eligible_groups: Patients undergoing treatment at designated apex hospitals (e.g., NIMHANS Bengaluru, AIIMS, PGIMER, Kidwai Memorial Institute)
income_criteria: Strictly limited to families living Below Poverty Line (BPL) as verified by state revenue authorities or valid BPL card.
beneficiary_requirements: Valid BPL Ration Card or certified income proof
Treating doctor's certificate and cost estimate from designated government institute
Patient must not be receiving duplicate benefits under PMJAY or other insurance schemes
covered_treatments: Cancer (surgical, chemotherapy, and radiotherapy interventions)
Major cardiac surgeries and congenital heart disease repairs
Kidney and liver transplants
Neurosurgical life-saving procedures
Severe hematological disorders (Thalassemia major, aplastic anemia)
benefits: One-time financial grant up to ₹15,00,000 released directly to the treating government super-specialty hospital for the patient's medical expenses.
limitations_and_exclusions: Treatment in private commercial hospitals is strictly excluded. Patients with active comprehensive insurance coverage or central government employee status are ineligible.
required_documents: Application in prescribed RAN Performa counter-signed by the treating specialist and Hospital Medical Superintendent
Attested copy of BPL Ration Card / Income Certificate
Detailed diagnostic reports, biopsy, CT/MRI scans, and clinical case summary
Cost breakdown estimate on official hospital letterhead
Aadhaar Card and two passport-sized photographs
application_steps: Step 1: Obtain initial diagnosis and treatment recommendation from a designated government super-specialty institute (e.g., NIMHANS or Kidwai in Bengaluru).
Step 2: Collect the official RAN application form from the hospital medical social worker (MSW) or superintendent office.
Step 3: Have the treating professor/HOD complete the clinical justification and estimated expenditure section.
Step 4: Attach attested copies of BPL card, Aadhaar, and diagnostic workups.
Step 5: Hospital forwards the dossier to the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare (MoHFW) RAN Technical Committee for grant sanction.
application_method: Through the Medical Superintendent / Social Welfare Officer of the treating designated government hospital.

short_description: Central financial assistance up to ₹1,25,000 for indigent patients with annual family income up to ₹1.25 Lakhs undergoing specialized treatment in government hospitals.
purpose: Provide discretionary financial aid to poor individuals who are not covered by other institutional schemes to defray immediate treatment costs.
geographical_coverage: Pan-India (Valid for treatments in government healthcare institutions).
eligible_groups: Low-income citizens undergoing major medical or surgical treatment in government hospitals
income_criteria: Total annual family income must not exceed ₹1,25,000 (verified by Tahsildar / Revenue Authority).
beneficiary_requirements: Income certificate verifying income below ₹1,25,000 per annum
Treatment underway in a Central or State Government hospital
Not eligible if covered under PM-JAY or reimbursement schemes
covered_treatments: Cardiovascular surgeries
Cancer treatment cycles
Orthopedic joint replacements and spinal surgeries
Kidney surgeries and related intervention
Major surgical procedures requiring specialized implants or drugs
benefits: Financial grant up to ₹1,25,000 disbursed directly to the concerned government hospital treasury for patient care.
limitations_and_exclusions: Excludes private hospitals, chronic long-term outpatient maintenance, and patients whose family income exceeds ₹1.25 Lakhs per year.
required_documents: Prescribed HMDG Application Form signed by Member of Parliament (MP) or treating doctor
Income Certificate issued by Tahsildar / Sub-Divisional Magistrate
Estimated cost certificate signed by treating government specialist
Aadhaar Card and proof of residence
application_steps: Step 1: Obtain the HMDG application format from the treating government hospital or download from MoHFW.
Step 2: Obtain an official income certificate (annual income under ₹1.25 Lakhs) from your local revenue office (Tahsildar).
Step 3: Have the treating doctor and Medical Superintendent fill the medical estimate section.
Step 4: Submit the completed dossier to the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi (or through the hospital administrative office).
Step 5: Ministry committee sanctions the grant and credits funds to the hospital's patient welfare account.
application_method: Postal or administrative submission to the Grants Section, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Nirman Bhawan, New Delhi.

scheme_name: Karnataka Chief Minister's Relief Fund - Medical Assistance (CMRF)
short_description: State discretionary medical grant providing financial assistance (typically ₹50,000 to ₹1,00,000+) for economically distressed Karnataka residents facing catastrophic diseases.
purpose: Provide timely humanitarian financial relief to needy families facing high treatment expenses for life-threatening illnesses in recognized hospitals.
eligible_groups: Permanent residents of Karnataka from economically weaker backgrounds
income_criteria: Economically weaker section; verified via family income certificate or BPL ration card.
beneficiary_requirements: Karnataka domicile or proof of continuous residence
Treatment for serious illness in a recognized government, trust, or authorized private hospital
Valid treatment quotation and clinical summary
covered_treatments: Heart surgery (valve replacement, CABG, pediatric cardiac corrections)
Cancer treatment (chemotherapy, radiation therapy, tumor resection)
Kidney failure and renal transplants
Brain surgery and neurological trauma
Major accidental trauma surgeries
benefits: One-time financial assistance check/electronic transfer (typically ₹25,000 up to ₹1,00,000 or higher based on committee evaluation) drawn in favor of the treating hospital.
limitations_and_exclusions: Discretionary grant subject to committee budget approval; not an open-ended cashless health insurance guarantee. Elective or minor procedures are ineligible.
required_documents: Original Medical Certificate and detailed cost estimation signed by treating physician
Valid Income Certificate (issued by Tahsildar / Revenue Department) or BPL Card
Aadhaar Card and proof of Karnataka residence
Hospital registration details, discharge summary (if already admitted), and original bills
application_steps: Step 1: Collect original medical certificate, diagnostic reports, and expenditure estimate from the treating recognized hospital.
Step 2: Obtain an Income Certificate from your local Nada Kacheri / Tahsildar office.
Step 3: Apply online through the Karnataka Seva Sindhu / CMRF portal or submit physical application at the Deputy Commissioner (DC) office or CM Secretariat, Vidhana Soudha, Bengaluru.
Step 4: The verification team scrutinizes the application and forwards it to the CMRF Medical Advisory Board.
Step 5: Sanction order is issued and the relief check/NEFT is transferred directly to the hospital's account.
application_method: Online via Karnataka Seva Sindhu / CMRF Portal, or in-person submission at the District Deputy Commissioner's Office or CM Secretariat.

scheme_name: National Policy for Rare Diseases (NPRD) Financial Support Scheme
short_description: Central financial support up to ₹50 Lakhs for patients suffering from diagnosed rare diseases for treatment at designated Centres of Excellence (including NIMHANS and IGICH in Bengaluru).
purpose: Provide comprehensive financial aid for specialized therapies, enzyme replacements, and curative interventions for documented rare genetic and metabolic diseases.
geographical_coverage: Pan-India (Treatment conducted at designated Centres of Excellence like NIMHANS and IGICH in Karnataka).
eligible_groups: Indian citizens diagnosed with documented rare diseases listed under NPRD Group 1, Group 2, or Group 3
income_criteria: Financial assistance up to ₹50 Lakhs is available for any patient suffering from specified rare disease categories regardless of income ceiling under the revised NPRD guidelines.
beneficiary_requirements: Formal clinical and genetic confirmation of rare disease at an empaneled Centre of Excellence (CoE)
CoE Rare Disease Committee recommendation and treatment protocol approval
covered_treatments: Lysosomal Storage Disorders (Gaucher disease, Pompe disease, MPS)
Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID)
Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA)
Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT) for inborn metabolic errors
Designated rare neurological and pediatric genetic disorders
benefits: One-time or phased financial support up to ₹50,00,000 managed and utilized directly by the Centre of Excellence hospital for medicines and therapeutic procedures.
limitations_and_exclusions: Assistance can only be availed at designated government Centres of Excellence (CoEs). Private non-CoE clinics cannot receive funding under this scheme.
required_documents: Genetic and biochemical test confirmation reports from accredited laboratory
Aadhaar Card and proof of Indian citizenship
Application form certified by the Nodal Officer of the Centre of Excellence
Treatment plan and cost projections drafted by the CoE Expert Committee
application_steps: Step 1: Patient visits a designated Centre of Excellence (e.g., NIMHANS or Indira Gandhi Institute of Child Health in Bengaluru).
Step 2: CoE clinical genetics unit carries out diagnostic confirmation and classification under NPRD groups.
Step 3: CoE Rare Disease Committee prepares clinical evaluation and estimated therapeutic costs.
Step 4: The CoE Nodal Officer uploads patient application and documentation onto the central MoHFW Rare Diseases crowdfunding portal.
Step 5: Ministry disburses the sanctioned amount directly to the Centre of Excellence for procuring orphan drugs and managing treatment.
application_method: Through the designated Centre of Excellence (CoE) Nodal Unit (NIMHANS / IGICH Bengaluru).

short_description: Free hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis services at government district hospitals for BPL patients suffering from end-stage renal failure.
purpose: Provide accessible, decentralized, and cashless life-sustaining renal replacement therapy in public health facilities.
geographical_coverage: Pan-India (Available across district hospitals in Karnataka including KC General and Bowring Hospital in Bengaluru).
eligible_groups: Patients diagnosed with Chronic Kidney Disease / End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) requiring ongoing dialysis
income_criteria: 100% Free for Below Poverty Line (BPL) cardholders; available at subsidized, capped government rates for non-BPL patients.
beneficiary_requirements: Confirmed nephrologist prescription indicating requirement for maintenance hemodialysis
BPL Ration card or Ayushman Bharat ID for 100% cashless waiver
Aadhaar Card
covered_treatments: Maintenance Hemodialysis cycles (multiple sessions weekly)
Peritoneal Dialysis consumables and support
Basic dialysis-related routine blood investigations at district units
benefits: Completely cashless hemodialysis sessions, dialyzer reuse, and nursing support at district hospital dialysis centers.
limitations_and_exclusions: Does not fund kidney transplantation surgeries directly (transplants are covered under AB-PMJAY/RAN). Limited to dialysis care units established under Public-Private Partnership (PPP) in government hospitals.
required_documents: Aadhaar Card
BPL / PHH Ration Card (or PMJAY / ArK card)
Nephrologist diagnosis card / Serum Creatinine and eGFR laboratory reports
Hepatitis B, C and HIV screening test results (mandatory for dialysis entry)
application_steps: Step 1: Obtain a nephrologist diagnosis slip and viral markers screening reports.
Step 2: Visit the PMNDP Dialysis Unit at the local district government hospital (e.g., KC General Hospital or Bowring Hospital in Bengaluru).
Step 3: Present your BPL card, Aadhaar, and medical records to the dialysis unit coordinator.
Step 4: Register in the National Dialysis Portal registry to obtain your Dialysis Beneficiary ID.
Step 5: Schedule your weekly maintenance dialysis slots for cashless sessions.
application_method: Walk-in registration at the dialysis center within designated government district hospitals.

short_description: Completely free delivery, C-section, medicines, diagnostics, food, and transport for all pregnant women and sick infants up to 1 year in public health facilities.
purpose: Eliminate all out-of-pocket expenses for pregnant women delivering in government health facilities and ensure immediate care for sick newborns.
geographical_coverage: Pan-India (Active across all public health centers and government maternity hospitals in Karnataka).
eligible_groups: All pregnant women delivering in public government health institutions
All sick neonates and infants up to 1 year of age receiving care at public hospitals
income_criteria: Universal entitlement. No income ceiling or ration card requirement; completely free for all mothers and infants in public facilities.
beneficiary_requirements: Admission to any government hospital (e.g., Vani Vilas Hospital, Bowring Hospital, Community Health Centres)
Mother and Child Tracking System (MCTS) / RCH ID registration
Mother's identification proof (Aadhaar / Voter ID)
covered_treatments: Normal vaginal delivery and emergency Cesarean sections
Free antenatal and intrapartum diagnostic tests (blood tests, ultrasounds)
Free inpatient medications, blood transfusions, and consumables
Free dietary meals during hospital stay (minimum 3 days for normal, 7 days for C-section)
Free ambulance transport from home to hospital and drop-back home
Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) treatment for sick infants up to 1 year
benefits: Zero out-of-pocket expenditure entitlement for institutional deliveries and neonatal care in government health setups.
limitations_and_exclusions: Applies exclusively to public government health facilities. Deliveries in private commercial nursing homes are not covered.
required_documents: Mother and Child Health (MCH) Card / Thayi Card (in Karnataka)
Aadhaar Card of mother
Bank passbook details (for linked maternity cash incentive under Janani Suraksha Yojana / PMMVY)
application_steps: Step 1: Register pregnancy at the nearest Urban Primary Health Centre (UPHC) or with the local ASHA worker to receive the Thayi Card / RCH ID.
Step 2: Attend regular free antenatal checkups at the public health center.
Step 3: At the onset of labor, call 108 for free ambulance transport to a government maternity hospital (such as Vani Vilas Hospital in Bengaluru).
Step 4: Present your Thayi Card and Aadhaar at admission; all diagnostics, medicines, and delivery care are provided with zero charges.
Step 5: Utilize free 102/108 drop-back vehicle service to return home safely after discharge.
application_method: Automatic entitlement upon admission at any government health facility / maternity hospital.

scheme_name: Nikshay Poshan Yojana (National TB Elimination Programme)
short_description: Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) of ₹500/month nutritional financial support directly into the bank accounts of all notified tuberculosis patients throughout treatment.
purpose: Provide nutritional support to TB patients to improve treatment compliance, nutritional status, and clinical recovery outcomes.
geographical_coverage: Pan-India (Administered via State TB Cells, including Karnataka State Tuberculosis Elimination Programme).
eligible_groups: All tuberculosis patients (drug-sensitive and drug-resistant) notified in the official Nikshay national portal
income_criteria: Universal entitlement for all notified TB patients irrespective of socioeconomic status or income level.
beneficiary_requirements: Notification of TB diagnosis on Nikshay portal by treating doctor / clinic
Active bank account linked to Aadhaar (for DBT transfers)
Ongoing compliance with anti-TB treatment regimen
covered_treatments: Pulmonary and Extra-Pulmonary Tuberculosis management
Drug-Resistant TB (MDR-TB / XDR-TB) courses
Free anti-TB medications (DOTS) provided alongside DBT payments
benefits: ₹500 per month credited directly to the beneficiary's bank account for each month of completed treatment, along with free diagnostic sputum tests and first-line/second-line TB drugs.
limitations_and_exclusions: Financial support requires valid Nikshay registration and bank account details; payments stop once treatment is clinically completed or defaulted.
required_documents: Aadhaar Card
Bank Account passbook copy (showing IFSC and Account Number) for Direct Benefit Transfer
Diagnostic report (CBNAAT / TrueNat / Sputum Microscopy) confirming TB
application_steps: Step 1: Undergo sputum or diagnostic testing at a Primary Health Centre, Designated Microscopy Centre, or private clinic.
Step 2: Ensure the clinic or TB Health Visitor (TBHV) enters your diagnosis on the national Nikshay portal (nikshay.in).
Step 3: Provide your Aadhaar number and active bank passbook details to the Nikshay coordinator.
Step 4: Receive free DOTS medication from the nearest government health center.
Step 5: Monthly cash transfer of ₹500 is credited directly to your bank account via PFMS until treatment completion.
application_method: Registration on Nikshay portal via the treating healthcare facility or local Senior Treatment Supervisor (STS).

short_description: Cashless surgical health insurance up to ₹5 Lakhs per family per year for members of rural and urban cooperative societies in Karnataka.
purpose: Provide affordable social health insurance protection against surgical hospitalization expenses to cooperative members, farmers, and weavers in Karnataka.
eligible_groups: Members of registered rural and urban cooperative societies in Karnataka
Members of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), milk producers' unions, and weavers' cooperatives
Spouse, children, and dependent parents of registered cooperative members
income_criteria: No specific income limit, but applicant must be an active registered member of a Karnataka cooperative society for at least 3 months.
beneficiary_requirements: Valid membership in a registered Karnataka cooperative society
Yeshasvini beneficiary card issued for the active financial year
Aadhaar Card
covered_treatments: General surgery, abdominal and laparoscopic procedures
Cardiac surgeries (CABG, valve replacement, pediatric cardiac surgery)
Orthopedic joint surgeries and complex trauma management
Gynecological surgeries (hysterectomy, ovarian cyst removal)
Urology and pediatric surgical packages (over 1,650 listed surgical procedures)
benefits: Cashless surgical treatment coverage up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year in empaneled private and government network hospitals across Karnataka.
limitations_and_exclusions: Medical admissions without surgical intervention, OPD treatments, cosmetic surgeries, and treatment at non-empaneled hospitals are excluded. Strictly limited to cooperative society members.
required_documents: Yeshasvini Health Card / Enrolment Receipt
Cooperative Society Membership Certificate / Passbook
Aadhaar Card of the patient
Treating surgeon's diagnosis note and surgical recommendation
application_steps: Step 1: Enroll during the annual registration window at your local cooperative society, DCC Bank branch, or online portal.
Step 2: Pay the nominal subsidized annual membership premium (e.g., ₹500 for rural, ₹1,000 for urban families).
Step 3: Receive your Yeshasvini UHID / Health Card.
Step 4: When surgical intervention is advised, visit an empaneled network hospital (e.g., Jayadeva, Narayana Health City, etc.).
Step 5: The hospital Yeshasvini coordinator uploads surgical pre-authorization for cashless clearance from the trust.
application_method: Enrolment through local cooperative society office / Karnataka Apex Bank / Seva Sindhu during enrolment drives.
